title: The Quiet Weather
premise: Ada Lockridge, a translator who has spent thirty years rendering other people's words while her mother tongue — a dying dialect from a coastal village — slips away word by word, returns to her hometown when the house she grew up in goes to public auction. The auction forces together the scattered remnants of her childhood found family: Marisol, the neighbor girl who became a stranger; Tomas, the foster brother who kept the house standing; and old Mrs. Vane, whose silence holds the truth about why Ada's family left. As Ada races to translate a single sentence her dying father wrote in the dialect — a sentence that determines who truly owns the house, and what happened the winter her sister disappeared — she must choose between loyalty to the family that raised her and the truth that could break them. In the end, Ada translates the sentence aloud at the auction: it names her sister alive and forgiven, and bequeaths the house not to any one of them but 'to whoever stays.' Ada stays.
about_author: Lena Coldharbour is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between two languages on a fading northern coastline. She writes about the words families lose before they learn they needed them.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the city, Ada works a translation job and realizes she can no longer recall the dialect word for 'home,' substituting the borrowed term without thinking. Her apartment feels rented even by her own life. Emotional beat: quiet dread of erasure.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A legal notice arrives: the Lockridge childhood house enters auction in six weeks, contested claims attached. Ada hasn't been back in fifteen years. She tells herself she'll go only to sign papers. Emotional beat: denial cracking into obligation.

chapters.title: The Road Back
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The bus ride along the coast; the village is smaller, saltier, half-abandoned. She passes the house and sees an auction placard nailed over the door where her height marks once were. Emotional beat: grief disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Tomas Keeps the Lights
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, the foster brother who never left, has quietly maintained the empty house for years — fixing the roof, paying taxes he couldn't afford. He sees Ada arrive and says nothing, only makes tea for two. Emotional beat: loyalty as silent devotion.

chapters.title: Marisol at the Counter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Ada finds Marisol running the village shop, brisk and armored, pretending fifteen years of silence were a choice. Their first conversation is all small talk over a counter that used to be a windowsill they climbed through. Emotional beat: tenderness under frost.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sorting her father's papers in the attic, Ada finds a page in the dialect — one sentence, unfinished-feeling, addressed to no one. Half its words have gone strange to her. It mentions the house, and her lost sister Ruth. Emotional beat: fascination shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: What Mrs. Vane Saw
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. The elderly neighbor watches Ada carry boxes and remembers the winter of 1989, when the Lockridge parents loaded the car at dawn and told everyone Ruth had gone to an aunt's. Mrs. Vane has kept one secret for thirty-five years. Emotional beat: guilt aging into stone.

chapters.title: Terms of the Estate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The lawyer explains: three claimants — Tomas, a distant cousin, and a developer — plus a clause Ada's father added: if a document in the family dialect can be authenticated and translated before the sale, the court must honor it. Six weeks. Emotional beat: hope arriving as a deadline.

chapters.title: Words That Won't Come
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada attempts the translation and fails; the dialect lives now only in three elderly speakers, and each gives her different words for the same phrase. Language, she realizes, was always communal — she cannot do this alone. Emotional beat: humility.

chapters.title: The Night We Buried the Radio
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Childhood memory: Ada, Ruth, Tomas, and Marisol burying a radio in the garden as a 'time capsule,' swearing loyalty. The last summer before everything broke. Emotional beat: golden warmth with a hairline crack.

chapters.title: Marisol's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals she has kept accounts since childhood — debts, favors, apologies owed. She shows Ada an entry from 1989: something the Lockridge parents asked her to keep quiet, payment made in groceries. Emotional beat: the cost of being trusted.

chapters.title: The Cousin Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The cousin, Gerald, arrives with surveyors and charm, offering buyouts. Tomas refuses; Marisol wavers, her shop drowning in debt. The found family's first real fracture. Emotional beat: money making honesty expensive.

chapters.title: Second Speaker
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada visits the second surviving speaker, old Ivo, who translates part of the sentence — and stops cold at one word, refusing to continue, saying only: 'Ask the woman who watched you leave.' Emotional beat: the past raising its hand.

chapters.title: Ruth Was Not Gone
chapters.summary: Mrs. Vane's POV. Under Ada's gentle pressure, Mrs. Vane begins to confess: Ruth didn't leave — after a fire in the boathouse, the frightened parents sent her away to relatives and swore the village to silence, ashamed. Mrs. Vane kept the address. Emotional beat: relief and fury entangled.

chapters.title: The Address
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada writes to the address; a reply comes — Ruth is alive, living two provinces away, and does not want the house or the past opened. Enclosed: a single line in the dialect, completing their father's sentence. Emotional beat: answer arriving as wound.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas confronts Ada: translating the sentence publicly will expose what the parents did, shaming the dead and breaking Marisol's lifelong secret-keeping. He asks her to let the house go instead. Emotional beat: love demanding silence.

chapters.title: The Garden Dig
chapters.summary: Ada, Tomas, and Marisol's shared POV sections. They dig up the time capsule radio; inside the casing, Ruth hid a note the others never knew — proof she forgave them even then. Marisol weeps for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: buried things surfacing.

chapters.title: Auction Eve
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The night before the auction, Ada finishes the full translation, checks every word against Ivo and Mrs. Vane, and understands the sentence whole: it names Ruth, forgives the silence, and leaves the house 'to whoever stays.' Emotional beat: clarity like cold water.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. At the auction, before bidding opens, Ada stands and reads the sentence aloud in the dying dialect, then in English. The room goes still. Gerald withdraws; the cousin's claim collapses; Ruth, arrived unannounced, hears herself named. Emotional beat: truth spoken at last.

chapters.title: To Whoever Stays
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ada's POV. The court honors the clause. No one sells. Ruth and Ada sit on the porch speaking broken dialect to each other, rebuilding the language between them like mending a net. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: New Words
chapters.summary: Marisol and Tomas's alternating POV. Spring: the house becomes something shared — Marisol's shop moves its back room in, Tomas finally sleeps under his own repaired roof. The found family, older and scarred, re-forms around the table. Emotional beat: quiet joy.

chapters.title: Owner, Not Tenant
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV. A year later, Ada translates a book in the revived dialect and teaches Sunday sessions in the kitchen. She writes the word for 'home' on the doorframe beside the old height marks. She is no longer a tenant of her own life. Emotional beat: arrival.
